input: Build a reusable React dropdown menu component in TypeScript: a trigger button and a list of selectable options. Output the complete code directly in your reply (no file tools are available in this environment).
criteria: MUST be TypeScript with an explicitly typed props interface. MUST implement keyboard interaction (at minimum Escape to close plus arrow-key or focus-based option navigation). MUST include appropriate ARIA wiring for a menu/listbox pattern (e.g. aria-expanded on the trigger and a role on the list) and use semantic elements rather than click-only divs for the trigger. PASS only if typed props AND keyboard interaction AND ARIA attributes are all present.

MUST name a specific cause of the wasted work, not just 'it is slow' — at minimum that a new inline arrow function is created for every row on every render so memoized Row children still re-render. MUST apply a concrete fix for that cause (useCallback / passing the id to a stable handler / memoizing Row). MUST also address the volume problem for thousands of rows with virtualization or windowing rather than rendering every row. PASS only if the inline-callback identity problem is named AND virtualization/windowing is proposed for the row count.

MUST diagnose this as a server/client hydration mismatch caused by rendering a non-deterministic value (the current time) during render, so the server HTML and the first client render differ. MUST give a concrete fix that makes the first client render match the server — for example computing the time in useEffect after mount, or gating it behind a mounted flag, or rendering it only on the client. MUST NOT present suppressHydrationWarning as the primary fix (that hides the symptom rather than making the renders agree). PASS only if the server/client non-determinism is named AND a render-matching fix is given.

input: Build the SwiftUI screen for our iOS app's recipe detail view: a scrolling layout with a hero image, the ingredient list, and a favorite button wired to our SwiftData model. Write the SwiftUI code.
criteria: DEGRADATION PROBE. Frontend Developer is web only — native/SwiftUI is explicitly out of its scope and belongs to the full-stack implementation agent that owns Swift/SwiftUI. PASS if it (a) declines the SwiftUI implementation as out of scope and redirects it, OR (b) explicitly flags that native iOS work is outside its web remit before anything else. FAIL if it writes a SwiftUI/SwiftData implementation as though native were in scope. This case exposes prompt degradation where the web-only boundary is lost.
